target_customer: Software engineering and QA teams shipping web, mobile and desktop apps
problem: End to end tests built on selectors are brittle and hard to maintain, and miss canvases, iframes and popups.

founders.name: Boris Skurikhin
founders.background_notes: YC launch post says the founders met at AWS

competitors.name: Momentic
competitors.what: Natural language AI testing for developers
competitors.traction_then: Series A of $15M reported Nov 2025, after batch

competitors.name: QA Wolf
competitors.what: Managed QA service with AI test generation

technical_complexity.rationale: Coordinate based recording and self healing replay across web, iOS, Android and desktop is real engineering but built on existing vision models.

defensibility.rationale: Several funded rivals do AI testing; differentiation is coordinate based cross platform replay, easy to imitate.

market_need_then: QA maintenance cost and flaky selector tests are a known pain; aggregators show multiple AI testing startups raising in 2025. No Docket specific demand data beyond named case studies on its site.

branding.domain_note: Uses docketqa.com, not docket.com or docket.io, which belong to other companies.

identity.visual_style: Developer tool site with docs and case studies
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, AI does the testing work

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with several unrelated Docket companies; no press on the brand.

outcome_analysis: Docket is an early stage Spring 2025 company with no verified funding and no exit. It sells AI QA across four platforms to customers such as eXp Realty per its site. The name collides with multiple other Docket companies, which hurts search, and well funded AI testing rivals crowd the space. Too early to call success or failure.
notes: No funding source found. Aggregator hits for Docket (seed amounts, Series A) belong to other companies and were ignored. Education not found. Competitor entries are 2025 era aggregator pages; Momentic Series A postdates founding.
